p.src:
S., in these lines, has Alpheus and Arethusa as mortals who are transformed into semi-di-
vinities through the destructive action of vanity and frustrated desire, incorporating Ovid’s
account of Alpheus’ pursuit of Arethusa, but breaking off before the two reach Sicily. GM
observes the extent to which S. is unsympathetic to Arethusa, no longer presented as
Alpheus’ innocent victim (as in Ovid), or as an unwilling bride (as in Pausanias), but rather
as a vain and conceited character; Alpheus, by contrast, is transformed from Ovid’s lustful
aggressor into a lovelorn victim (Stand v (1961) 2–3). GM suggests that S. took the hint for
this altered perspective from Met.: ‘Ovid had hinted that Arethusa was rather prudish (she
says, “crimque placere putavi” — “I thought it wrong to be attractive” [Met. v 584]), and
Shelley disliked prudery as much as he did vanity’. S. evidently did not intend this version of

u.src:
S., in these lines, has Alpheus and Arethusa as mortals who are transformed into semi-di-
vinities through the destructive action of vanity and frustrated desire, incorporating Ovid’s
account of Alpheus’ pursuit of Arethusa, but breaking off before the two reach Sicily.

ja: GMは、S. がアレトゥーサにどれほど
はもはや、オウィディウスにおけるアルペイオスの
でも、パウサニアスにおける
してアルペイオスは、オウィディウスの
u.src:
GM
observes the extent to which S. is unsympathetic to Arethusa, no longer presented as
Alpheus’ innocent victim (as in Ovid), or as an unwilling bride (as in Pausanias), but rather
as a vain and conceited character; Alpheus, by contrast, is transformed from Ovid’s lustful
aggressor into a lovelorn victim (Stand v (1961) 2–3).

ja: している。「オウィディウスは、アレトゥーサがかなり
であったことをほのめかしていた。
は “crimque placere putavi” すなわち『
u.src:
GM suggests that S. took the hint for
this altered perspective from Met.: ‘Ovid had hinted that Arethusa was rather prudish (she
says, “crimque placere putavi” — “I thought it wrong to be attractive” [Met.

v 584]), and
Shelley disliked prudery as much as he did vanity’.
S. evidently did not intend this version of

p.src:
the story for Proserpine; whether he ever conceived its publication, or whether it was simply
a jeu d’esprit, remains unknown.
